title: Intelligent Agents Actively Assist in Timing Decision-Making Guided by Cognitive State Confidence
content: We present confidence-guided sequential assistance (CGSA), an interface from electroencephalography (EEG) condition probabilities to optional assistance timing. Spectral features, random-forest estimation, smoothing, and held-out calibration feed a cost-derived admission bound with consecutive-window persistence and deadline abstention. Participant-disjoint replay uses 72 rest and arithmetic episodes from 36 participants, comprising 2,088 windows. The smoothed estimator reaches area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.710 and Brier score 0.219. Main-setting offers occur in 13/36 rest and 3/36 arithmetic episodes. Mean proxy cost is 0.534 versus 0.648 for a calibrated single-window gate and 0.500 for abstention; the paired difference interval includes zero. A 240-setting sensitivity analysis exposes dependence on temporal parameters and assigned costs. Fold diagnostics distinguish insufficient threshold crossings from weak participant transfer. At 16 stopping times, mean rest probability is 0.899 versus observed rest fraction 0.813, with substantial uncertainty. These results evaluate a controlled condition-based gate; practical interruption suitability and assistance benefit require interactive validation.
